挺.when: Remember 挺 like the word you’ll use when “quite” is enough — the interview questions were 挺容易的, not 非常难.
挺.usage: Most Chinese speakers wrap it as 挺……的 after an adjective. It’s spoken “pretty / rather,” a notch softer than 很.

example.zh: 还可以，他们问的问题都挺容易的，就是我有点儿紧张。
example.pinyin: Hái kěyǐ, tāmen wèn de wèntí dōu tǐng róngyì de, jiù shì wǒ yǒudiǎnr jǐnzhāng.
example.en: Pretty good — the questions they asked were all quite easy, it's just that I was a little nervous.

紧张.when: Remember 紧张 like the word you’ll use when your stomach drops before an interview — or when the calendar is packed.
紧张.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it two ways in this lesson: nerves (我有点儿紧张) and a tight schedule (时间安排得很紧张).

example.zh: 还可以，他们问的问题都挺容易的，就是我有点儿紧张。
example.pinyin: Hái kěyǐ, tāmen wèn de wèntí dōu tǐng róngyì de, jiù shì wǒ yǒudiǎnr jǐnzhāng.
example.en: Pretty good — the questions they asked were all quite easy, it's just that I was a little nervous.

信心.when: Remember 信心 like the word you’ll use when you tell someone to trust themselves before they walk into the 面试.
信心.usage: Most Chinese speakers say 对自己有信心 — confidence you hold, not a verb. This 课文 pairs it with 相信自己的能力.

example.zh: 面试的时候，一定要对自己有信心，要相信自己的能力。
example.pinyin: Miànshì de shíhou, yídìng yào duì zìjǐ yǒu xìnxīn, yào xiāngxìn zìjǐ de nénglì.
example.en: When you interview, you must have confidence in yourself and believe in your own ability.

能力.when: Remember 能力 like the word you’ll use when a manager asks whether someone can actually do the job.
能力.usage: Most Chinese speakers mean competence, not just “can.” In this lesson: 相信自己的能力, then 能力符合要求.

example.zh: 面试的时候，一定要对自己有信心，要相信自己的能力。
example.pinyin: Miànshì de shíhou, yídìng yào duì zìjǐ yǒu xìnxīn, yào xiāngxìn zìjǐ de nénglì.
example.en: When you interview, you must have confidence in yourself and believe in your own ability.

招聘.when: Remember 招聘 like the word you’ll use when a company is hiring — the 招聘会 at the gym, the 招聘工作 on Xiao Li’s desk.
招聘.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it from the employer side. They 招聘; you 应聘. 招聘会 is the job fair built on this verb.

example.zh: 你说的对！3月15号上午8点在学校体育馆还有一个招聘会，你去吗？
example.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de duì! Sānyuè shíwǔ hào shàngwǔ bā diǎn zài xuéxiào tǐyùguǎn hái yǒu yí ge zhāopìnhuì, nǐ qù ma?
example.en: You're right! There's another job fair at the school gym at 8am on March 15th — are you going?

提供.when: Remember 提供 like the word you’ll use when a job fair is offering posts — 提供工作机会 — not handing you a gift.
提供.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it for “provide / offer” (opportunities, materials, a suggestion). Formal than 给.

example.zh: 听说这次招聘会提供的工作机会很多，我们一起去看看吧。
example.pinyin: Tīngshuō zhè cì zhāopìnhuì tígōng de gōngzuò jīhuì hěn duō, wǒmen yìqǐ qù kànkan ba.
example.en: I heard this job fair offers a lot of job opportunities — let's go take a look together.

小雨.when: Remember 小雨 as the classmate in 课文1 — the one who just walked out of an interview and wants you at the 招聘会.
小雨.usage: Treat it as a person’s name. Don’t translate “little rain.” In this lesson it is only a speaker label plus the 课文 heading.

example.zh: 小夏和小雨聊小雨面试的情况
example.pinyin: Xiǎo Xià hé Xiǎoyǔ liáo Xiǎoyǔ miànshì de qíngkuàng
example.en: Xiao Xia and Xiao Yu talk about Xiao Yu's interview

负责.when: Remember 负责 like the word you’ll use when the manager asks who is running this 招聘.
负责.usage: Most Chinese speakers say 负责 + the task. 小李负责这次招聘 — then it gets handed to 小林.

example.zh: 小林，这次招聘不是小李负责吗？
example.pinyin: Xiǎo Lín, zhè cì zhāopìn bú shì Xiǎo Lǐ fùzé ma?
example.en: Xiao Lin, isn't Xiao Li in charge of this recruitment?

本来.when: Remember 本来 like the word you’ll use when the plan was Xiao Li’s job — and then he landed in hospital.
本来.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it for “originally / it should have been.” 本来是小李负责的, then 但是….

example.zh: 本来是小李负责的，但是他突然生病住院了，所以就交给我来做了。
example.pinyin: Běnlái shì Xiǎo Lǐ fùzé de, dànshì tā tūrán shēng bìng zhù yuàn le, suǒyǐ jiù jiāogěi wǒ lái zuò le.
example.en: It was originally Xiao Li's responsibility, but he suddenly fell ill and was hospitalized, so it was handed over to me to do.

应聘.when: Remember 应聘 like the word you’ll use when you are the one walking in — 15 people 来应聘, not the company 招聘.
应聘.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it from the applicant side. 应聘的人 / 应聘时不要紧张.

example.zh: 哦，这次应聘的人多吗？
example.pinyin: Ò, zhè cì yìngpìn de rén duō ma?
example.en: Oh, are there many people applying this time?

材料.when: Remember 材料 like the word you’ll use when you hand the manager the CVs after 笔试 and 面试.
材料.usage: Most Chinese speakers mean the file / documents here, not bricks or “building materials.” 这是他们的材料.

example.zh: 经理，这次来应聘的一共有15人。经过笔试和面试，有两个不错。这是他们的材料，您看看。
example.pinyin: Jīnglǐ, zhè cì lái yìngpìn de yígòng yǒu shíwǔ rén. Jīngguò bǐshì hé miànshì, yǒu liǎng ge búcuò. Zhè shì tāmen de cáiliào, nín kànkan.
example.en: Manager, a total of 15 people applied this time. After the written test and interview, two of them are quite good. Here are their materials — please take a look.

符合.when: Remember 符合 like the word you’ll use when someone’s ability actually matches what the job asks for.
符合.usage: Most Chinese speakers say 符合要求 / 符合条件 — “fits the standard,” not “agrees in an argument.”

example.zh: 这两个人的能力都比较符合我们的要求。你通知他们下周一上午九点来我办公室吧。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge rén de nénglì dōu bǐjiào fúhé wǒmen de yāoqiú. Nǐ tōngzhī tāmen xià zhōuyī shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn lái wǒ bàngōngshì ba.
example.en: Both of these people's abilities fit our requirements fairly well. Let them know to come to my office at 9am next Monday.

通知.when: Remember 通知 like the word you’ll use when you tell the two good candidates to come at nine — or when the manager says you start tomorrow.
通知.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it as a verb (通知他们) and as a noun (一份通知). This 课文 is the verb.

example.zh: 这两个人的能力都比较符合我们的要求。你通知他们下周一上午九点来我办公室吧。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge rén de nénglì dōu bǐjiào fúhé wǒmen de yāoqiú. Nǐ tōngzhī tāmen xià zhōuyī shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn lái wǒ bàngōngshì ba.
example.en: Both of these people's abilities fit our requirements fairly well. Let them know to come to my office at 9am next Monday.

马.when: Remember 马 as the family name on 马经理 — the boss asking who is running this 招聘.
马.usage: Treat it as a surname. Don’t translate “horse.” No 课文 line uses 马 as the name; 马上 in 课文2 is a different word.

example.zh: 马经理和小林聊招聘的事情
example.pinyin: Mǎ jīnglǐ hé Xiǎo Lín liáo zhāopìn de shìqing
example.en: Manager Ma and Xiao Lin talk about the recruitment

律师.when: Remember 律师 like the word you’ll use when Wang Jing says what she became the moment she graduated — 当律师 in Shanghai.
律师.usage: Most Chinese speakers mean a practicing lawyer. 当律师 is the job; 法律 is the subject she studied.

example.zh: 我一毕业就去上海当律师了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yí bìyè jiù qù Shànghǎi dāng lǜshī le.
example.en: As soon as I graduated I went to Shanghai to work as a lawyer.

专业.when: Remember 专业 like the word you’ll use when the job matches what you studied — 法律专业, so the work fits.
专业.usage: Most Chinese speakers mean a university major, or “this is my specialty.” 学的就是法律专业.

example.zh: 我很喜欢现在的工作，因为我学的就是法律专业，而且同事们都很喜欢我。另外，收入也不错。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan xiànzài de gōngzuò, yīnwèi wǒ xué de jiù shì fǎlǜ zhuānyè, érqiě tóngshìmen dōu hěn xǐhuan wǒ. Lìngwài, shōurù yě búcuò.
example.en: I really like my current job, because what I studied was law, and my colleagues all like me too. Besides, the income isn't bad either.

另外.when: Remember 另外 like the word you’ll use when the good news isn’t finished — job, colleagues, 另外 the pay.
另外.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it as “besides / and another thing” between sentences. It can also mean “another (one).” This 课文 is the conjunction.

example.zh: 我很喜欢现在的工作，因为我学的就是法律专业，而且同事们都很喜欢我。另外，收入也不错。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan xiànzài de gōngzuò, yīnwèi wǒ xué de jiù shì fǎlǜ zhuānyè, érqiě tóngshìmen dōu hěn xǐhuan wǒ. Lìngwài, shōurù yě búcuò.
example.en: I really like my current job, because what I studied was law, and my colleagues all like me too. Besides, the income isn't bad either.

收入.when: Remember 收入 like the word you’ll use when you add the money part after you already said you like the work.
收入.usage: Most Chinese speakers mean pay / income. 收入也不错 — not the verb “to receive a letter.”

example.zh: 我很喜欢现在的工作，因为我学的就是法律专业，而且同事们都很喜欢我。另外，收入也不错。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan xiànzài de gōngzuò, yīnwèi wǒ xué de jiù shì fǎlǜ zhuānyè, érqiě tóngshìmen dōu hěn xǐhuan wǒ. Lìngwài, shōurù yě búcuò.
example.en: I really like my current job, because what I studied was law, and my colleagues all like me too. Besides, the income isn't bad either.

咱们.when: Remember 咱们 like the word you’ll use when you include the person you’re talking to — Sunday, 咱们 classmate reunion.
咱们.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 咱们 for “we, including you.” 我们 can leave the listener out.

example.zh: 星期天咱们同学聚会，你能来参加吗？
example.pinyin: Xīngqītiān zánmen tóngxué jùhuì, nǐ néng lái cānjiā ma?
example.en: We're having a classmates' get-together on Sunday — can you come?

安排.when: Remember 安排 like the word you’ll use when the timetable is the problem — 时间安排得很紧张 on this Beijing trip.
安排.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it as a verb (安排时间) and for the plan itself. Here the schedule is tight, not “nervous.”

example.zh: 能来。虽然这次来北京，时间安排得很紧张，但我一定借这次机会去跟大家见见面。
example.pinyin: Néng lái. Suīrán zhè cì lái Běijīng, shíjiān ānpái de hěn jǐnzhāng, dàn wǒ yídìng jiè zhè cì jīhuì qù gēn dàjiā jiànjian miàn.
example.en: I can come. Although my schedule on this trip to Beijing is very tight, I'll definitely take this opportunity to meet up with everyone.

首先.when: Remember 首先 like the word you’ll use when you start the interview list — first, wear formal clothes.
首先.usage: Most Chinese speakers pair it with 其次 in writing. Alone it also means “first of all / the first thing you do.”

example.zh: 首先，要穿正式的衣服，这会给面试者留下一个好的印象，让他觉得你是一个认真的人。
example.pinyin: Shǒuxiān, yào chuān zhèngshì de yīfu, zhè huì gěi miànshìzhě liúxià yí ge hǎo de yìnxiàng, ràng tā juéde nǐ shì yí ge rènzhēn de rén.
example.en: First, wear formal clothing — this will leave the interviewer with a good impression and make them feel you're a conscientious person.

正式.when: Remember 正式 like the word you’ll use when the interview needs a real outfit, not weekend clothes.
正式.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it for formal dress, a formal job, a formal start date. 穿正式的衣服.

example.zh: 首先，要穿正式的衣服，这会给面试者留下一个好的印象，让他觉得你是一个认真的人。
example.pinyin: Shǒuxiān, yào chuān zhèngshì de yīfu, zhè huì gěi miànshìzhě liúxià yí ge hǎo de yìnxiàng, ràng tā juéde nǐ shì yí ge rènzhēn de rén.
example.en: First, wear formal clothing — this will leave the interviewer with a good impression and make them feel you're a conscientious person.

留.when: Remember 留 like the word you’ll use when you leave an impression behind — 留下一个好的印象 in formal clothes.
留.usage: Most Chinese speakers say 留下印象 / 留在家里. This lesson is “leave (an impression),” not “stay and study.”

example.zh: 首先，要穿正式的衣服，这会给面试者留下一个好的印象，让他觉得你是一个认真的人。
example.pinyin: Shǒuxiān, yào chuān zhèngshì de yīfu, zhè huì gěi miànshìzhě liúxià yí ge hǎo de yìnxiàng, ràng tā juéde nǐ shì yí ge rènzhēn de rén.
example.en: First, wear formal clothing — this will leave the interviewer with a good impression and make them feel you're a conscientious person.

其次.when: Remember 其次 like the word you’ll use when 首先 is done — second, don’t be nervous when you 应聘.
其次.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it to number the next point, usually after 首先, more on the page than in chat.

example.zh: 其次，应聘时不要紧张。
example.pinyin: Qícì, yìngpìn shí búyào jǐnzhāng.
example.en: Second, don't be nervous when interviewing.

诚实.when: Remember 诚实 like the word you’ll use when the book says the most important interview rule is to tell the truth.
诚实.usage: Most Chinese speakers describe a person or an answer as 诚实 — honest, not 认真 (conscientious) and not “frank.”

example.zh: 当然，最重要的是回答问题要诚实。
example.pinyin: Dāngrán, zuì zhòngyào de shì huídá wèntí yào chéngshí.
example.en: Of course, the most important thing is to be honest when answering questions.

改变.when: Remember 改变 like the word you’ll use when a first impression is already set — and changing it is hard.
改变.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it for changing a situation or an impression, not changing clothes (换).

example.zh: 虽然第一印象不总是对的，但如果想改变却很困难。
example.pinyin: Suīrán dì yī yìnxiàng bù zǒng shì duì de, dàn rúguǒ xiǎng gǎibiàn què hěn kùnnan.
example.en: Although a first impression isn't always correct, it is very hard to change if you want to.

感觉.when: Remember 感觉 like the word you’ll use when a first impression shapes how people feel about you later.
感觉.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it as a noun (感觉和判断) and as “I feel that….” This 课文 is the noun.

example.zh: 你给别人的第一印象会影响他们以后对你的感觉和判断。
example.pinyin: Nǐ gěi biérén de dì yī yìnxiàng huì yǐngxiǎng tāmen yǐhòu duì nǐ de gǎnjué hé pànduàn.
example.en: The first impression you give others will affect their feelings about and judgment of you afterward.

判断.when: Remember 判断 like the word you’ll use when someone sizes you up after that first meeting.
判断.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it as a verb and a noun. This 课文 is 感觉和判断 — the judgment they form about you.

example.zh: 你给别人的第一印象会影响他们以后对你的感觉和判断。
example.pinyin: Nǐ gěi biérén de dì yī yìnxiàng huì yǐngxiǎng tāmen yǐhòu duì nǐ de gǎnjué hé pànduàn.
example.en: The first impression you give others will affect their feelings about and judgment of you afterward.

顾客.when: Remember 顾客 like the word you’ll use when a good first impression might mean you sell more.
顾客.usage: Most Chinese speakers mean a customer in a shop or business, not a house guest (客人) and not a colleague.

example.zh: 所以，给第一次见面的同事留下好的印象，以后的工作可能会更顺利；给第一次见面的顾客留下好的印象，你可能会卖出更多的东西。
example.pinyin: Suǒyǐ, gěi dì yī cì jiàn miàn de tóngshì liúxià hǎo de yìnxiàng, yǐhòu de gōngzuò kěnéng huì gèng shùnlì; gěi dì yī cì jiàn miàn de gùkè liúxià hǎo de yìnxiàng, nǐ kěnéng huì màichū gèng duō de dōngxi.
example.en: So, leaving a good impression on a colleague you meet for the first time may make future work go more smoothly; leaving a good impression on a customer you meet for the first time may let you sell more goods.

准时.when: Remember 准时 like the word you’ll use when being on time is the whole point — class, work, or a 约会.
准时.usage: Most Chinese speakers praise a person as 准时, or say 准时出发. The bad first impression in this 课文 is 不准时.

example.zh: 所以不管是上课、上班，还是与别人约会，准时都非常重要。
example.pinyin: Suǒyǐ bùguǎn shì shàng kè, shàng bān, háishi yǔ biérén yuēhuì, zhǔnshí dōu fēicháng zhòngyào.
example.en: So whether it's attending class, going to work, or meeting someone for an appointment, being punctual is extremely important.

不管.when: Remember 不管 like the word you’ll use when the result doesn’t change — class, work, or dating, 准时 still matters.
不管.usage: Most Chinese speakers pair it with 都 / 还是 / 什么. 不管是A还是B，…都….

example.zh: 所以不管是上课、上班，还是与别人约会，准时都非常重要。
example.pinyin: Suǒyǐ bùguǎn shì shàng kè, shàng bān, háishi yǔ biérén yuēhuì, zhǔnshí dōu fēicháng zhòngyào.
example.en: So whether it's attending class, going to work, or meeting someone for an appointment, being punctual is extremely important.

与.when: Remember 与 like the word you’ll use when you need a written “with” — 与别人约会.
与.usage: Most Chinese speakers say 跟 / 和 out loud. 与 is the same “with,” more formal or on the page.

example.zh: 所以不管是上课、上班，还是与别人约会，准时都非常重要。
example.pinyin: Suǒyǐ bùguǎn shì shàng kè, shàng bān, háishi yǔ biérén yuēhuì, zhǔnshí dōu fēicháng zhòngyào.
example.en: So whether it's attending class, going to work, or meeting someone for an appointment, being punctual is extremely important.

约会.en: to date, to go to an appointment
约会.when: Remember 约会 like the word you’ll use when you arranged to meet someone — a date or any appointment you must not be late for.
约会.usage: Most Chinese speakers use it for a romantic date and for “we have an appointment.” This 课文 pairs it with 准时.

example.zh: 所以不管是上课、上班，还是与别人约会，准时都非常重要。
example.pinyin: Suǒyǐ bùguǎn shì shàng kè, shàng bān, háishi yǔ biérén yuēhuì, zhǔnshí dōu fēicháng zhòngyào.
example.en: So whether it's attending class, going to work, or meeting someone for an appointment, being punctual is extremely important.

面试.when: Remember 面试 like the word you’ll use when you sit across from the manager and they ask the questions.
面试.usage: Most Chinese speakers mean the job interview, after 笔试. Noun or verb: 参加面试 / 面试的时候.

example.zh: 你上午的面试怎么样？
example.pinyin: Nǐ shàngwǔ de miànshì zěnmeyàng?
example.en: How was your interview this morning?

笔试.when: Remember 笔试 like the word you’ll use when the company tests you on paper before they talk to you.
笔试.usage: Most Chinese speakers contrast it with 面试. 经过笔试和面试 — written first, then the conversation.

example.zh: 经理，这次来应聘的一共有15人。经过笔试和面试，有两个不错。这是他们的材料，您看看。
example.pinyin: Jīnglǐ, zhè cì lái yìngpìn de yígòng yǒu shíwǔ rén. Jīngguò bǐshì hé miànshì, yǒu liǎng ge búcuò. Zhè shì tāmen de cáiliào, nín kànkan.
example.en: Manager, a total of 15 people applied this time. After the written test and interview, two of them are quite good. Here are their materials — please take a look.

体育馆.when: Remember 体育馆 like the word you’ll use when the job fair is in the school gym, not a classroom.
体育馆.usage: Most Chinese speakers mean a gymnasium / indoor stadium. 学校体育馆 is where this 招聘会 is held.

example.zh: 你说的对！3月15号上午8点在学校体育馆还有一个招聘会，你去吗？
example.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de duì! Sānyuè shíwǔ hào shàngwǔ bā diǎn zài xuéxiào tǐyùguǎn hái yǒu yí ge zhāopìnhuì, nǐ qù ma?
example.en: You're right! There's another job fair at the school gym at 8am on March 15th — are you going?

印象.when: Remember 印象 like the word you’ll use when the manager walks away thinking you’re 不错 — or when you talk about a first impression.
印象.usage: Most Chinese speakers say 对…印象不错 or 留下一个好的印象. This lesson’s title is that sentence. The JSON filed the 生词 under Lesson 1.

example.zh: 面试的时候，经理对我印象不错，还通知我明天就可以上班了。
example.pinyin: Miànshì de shíhou, jīnglǐ duì wǒ yìnxiàng búcuò, hái tōngzhī wǒ míngtiān jiù kěyǐ shàng bān le.
example.en: During the interview, the manager formed a good impression of me, and even told me I could start work tomorrow.
